spec.scenario_text: A plane electromagnetic wave reaches a flat boundary between two lossless media at normal incidence. The wave impedances on the incident and transmitted sides are independently varied, and the reflected fraction of incident power is measured. The target is the instantaneous algebraic power-reflection fraction at the interface. The benchmark isolates boundary matching of electric and magnetic wave amplitudes.

response_change.parent_relation: The reflected power depends only on the impedance ratio through R_P=((Z_2-Z_1)/(Z_2+Z_1))^2, so all experiments with the same Z_1 and Z_2 collapse to one curve independent of any surrounding condition.
response_change.child_relation: Add dependence on a finite-thickness interlayer condition so the net reflected power is set by interference between the front- and back-interface reflections, making the mapping depend jointly on impedance contrast and the added layer condition rather than on Z_1 and Z_2 alone.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed Z_1 and Z_2, the reflected fraction can vary from near zero to enhanced reflection as the added environmental condition changes, whereas the parent predicts one invariant value.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, varying the added layer condition while holding Z_1 and Z_2 fixed reveals non-collapsing reflected-power responses; in holdout, the same interference mechanism extends to new impedance contrasts and different phase thicknesses.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the added layer vanishes, when its rear-interface reflection tends to zero, or when coherence is lost so the extra contribution no longer affects the measured instantaneous algebraic reflection fraction.

plan.gap_statement: The model omits the realistic case of a thin matching or coating layer, so it cannot represent interference-modified reflection at otherwise normal incidence between lossless media.

plan.rationale: The parent target mapping is the single-interface Fresnel law: varying Z_2/Z_1 at fixed normal incidence gives one symmetric monotone mismatch response with a zero only at Z_1=Z_2. A natural next refinement is to insert a lossless finite layer, which changes the scored target itself, not just an auxiliary trajectory: the net reflected power now depends on both impedance mismatch and interlayer phase. Distinguishing condition: hold Z_1 and Z_2 fixed and vary the added layer condition over a phase range spanning roughly 0 to pi; the child predicts oscillatory suppression or enhancement of reflection, including anti-reflection points for some mismatched terminal impedances, while the parent with any single parameter set still predicts one constant reflected fraction for those same fixed Z_1 and Z_2. This is observable only when reflections from both interfaces are coherent and non-negligible; if the extra boundary is absent or effectively invisible, the refinement correctly collapses back to the parent.

evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the zero-loss limit of the interlayer, where round-trip attenuation tends to unity and the propagation factor becomes purely phase.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: attenuated internal multiple reflection in a coherent interlayer
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Weak absorption or finite conductivity in the interlayer causes the internal round-trip factor to decay in magnitude as well as rotate in phase, damping Fabry-Perot interference in the reflected power.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the attenuation multiplies the already nonlinear internal reflection pathway, simultaneously altering the interference term and recycled reflected contribution in a phase-dependent rational law rather than just rescaling the final output.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The parent assumes the interlayer medium is lossless, giving a purely real wave impedance and a purely phase-valued round-trip propagation factor.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The interlayer can be weakly attenuating, so the internal round-trip factor has magnitude below unity and modulates the coherent return amplitude.
